a: Innate immunity is the fast, general first line of defense.
Adaptive immunity is specific and forms memory.
Antigens are molecules recognized by the immune system.
Antibodies bind antigens with high specificity.
Boosters reinforce immune memory over time.
Antibiotics target bacteria; antivirals target viruses.
The microbiome is the community of microbes living on/in a host.
Negative feedback loops stabilize internal conditions.
Circadian rhythms are roughly 24-hour biological cycles.
Ecological succession is community change over time after disturbance.
